text.en: A young man from a small Tamil Nadu town filled notebooks with mathematical results that amazed Cambridge.

The lesson is a biography of the mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan. Working with G. H. Hardy at Cambridge, he made discoveries in number theory, partitions and continued fractions. He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society on 28 February 1918 as the youngest Indian to receive the honour, and in October that year became the first Indian elected a Fellow of Trinity College.
Ramanujan's story shows how passion, hard work and the right opportunity can lift a gifted person from humble beginnings. His birthday, 22 December, is celebrated in India as National Mathematics Day.
Learn biography words: fellow, elected, distinguished, achievement, identities and circle method. Note the use of dates and the past tense.
